 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Miami Heat landed Giannis Antetokounmpo over the summer in the latest Pat Riley move geared toward going all-in to win a championship. An 0-4 start to the season was not what the organization had in mind.
 The Heat did improve to 1-4 on Wednesday with a victory over the Atlanta Hawks and are at home Friday night against the Indiana Pacers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Insider Notes the Price Heat Paid for Giannis Antetokounmpo
 The slow start has led to rumors of the Heat adding another star, such as Kyrie Irving. However, NBA insider Brett Siegel shut down those rumors due to the harsh reality facing the Heat.
 The Heat sent Milwaukee four players – Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakučionis – along with three first-round picks, a 2030 first-round pick swap and a 2033 second-round pick in the Antetokounmpo trade.
 Siegel argued that Miami no longer has young talent with enough trade value to entice Dallas in an Irving deal. He appeared on his "Clutch Scoops" show and explained why the Heat are likely going to be unable to land a player such as Irving.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "You can monitor him all you want," Siegel said about Irving. "But this team gave up their draft capital for Giannis Antetokounmpo, they have no young talents that they can really trade away that would be of value to Dallas, and your package is basically Andrew Wiggins, who is on the declining end of his career in terms of what we've seen from him this season."
 The marquee players on the Heat are all older in NBA terms. Antetokounmpo is 31, Klay Thompson is 36, Andrew Wiggins is 31, and Bam Adebayo is 29 . Even Davion Mitchell is 28, and Siegel questioned whether a package featuring him, Wiggins and a future first-round pick would be competitive enough for a younger Dallas team.
 "Maybe you could throw in Davion Mitchell," Siegel continued. "That's a somewhat young piece that is having a good start to the season. And you could maybe offer your 2029 first-round pick if you took the 27 protections of what you offered to Charlotte and what they currently own. But is that better than what other teams out there can offer for Kyrie Irving?"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The time for the Heat to consider such a move was back in the summer before so much capital was traded to Milwaukee. Now, the team has hitched itself to Antetokounmpo and company.
 Siegel also went on to explain how a package for Irving would involve a series of draft picks, such as what the Heat sent to the Bucks for Antetokounmpo.
 "They may want to monitor him and watch him all they want and dream about pairing him with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, I just don't see any scenario in which that happens."

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This means, barring a miracle, the Heat will have to simply turn things around with the current roster in Miami. A win Friday night over the Pacers would be a good first step in that direction.
